prompt: What happens if an LGA1700 processor is forced into an AM5 motherboard socket?
options: The system will downclock to compatibility mode
The pins on the AM5 socket will be crushed and permanently damaged
The computer boots but memory channels are disabled
The UEFI BIOS will flash an error code on screen
explanation: LGA sockets feature delicate spring contact pins on the motherboard. Forcing an incompatible package will permanently crush the socket pins.

prompt: When installing two sticks of RAM on a standard 4-slot motherboard, which slot configuration is recommended by manufacturers?
options: Any arbitrary pair of adjacent slots
explanation: Modern daisy-chain memory trace topology terminates at the end of each trace (slots 2 and 4 / A2 and B2). Using these slots minimizes electrical stub reflections.

prompt: What is the consequence of forgetting to plug in the 8-pin EPS 12V cable to the top corner of the motherboard?
options: The computer will run at reduced CPU power
Fans and LEDs may turn on, but the CPU receives no VCore power and system cannot POST
Only integrated graphics will be disabled
Storage drives will not spin up
explanation: The 24-pin ATX connector powers chipset, RAM, and PCIe slots, while the 8-pin EPS specifically feeds the CPU VRM stages. Without EPS, the CPU is completely unpowered.
